newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Old Mutual backs offshore asset investment.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Old Mutual backs offshore asset investment.

text.p: Old Mutual, South Africa's biggest investment group, said on Friday the country's investors needed to increasingly move into foreign investments, taking advantage of the recent relaxation of foreign exchange controls.
The March 12 budget gave institutions the go ahead to invest up to 10 percent of their total assets abroad and not, as before, 10 percent of each individual mutual fund, known locally as unit trusts.

Kevin Carter, chief executive of Old Mutual Asset Managers U.K (OMAM), told a meeting on Friday that 35 percent of the $3.7 billion under management of OMAM represented assets owned by South Africans who had benefited from the asset swap concession.
Looking at offshore investment avenues he said European equities were set to deliver superior returns in world markets, while Latin America remained OMAM's favoured emerging market region.
"Low interest rates, low inflation and competitive currencies are stimulating a recovery across European economies," Carter said.
"(Latin America) does not suffer from the uncompetitive currencies which are causing problems for Asia's exporters," he added.
He said OMAM liked the look of the U.S. financial and technology sectors, while financial stocks in the U.K and continental Europe were also in favour.
In Japan, however, a weighting in favour of capital equipment and consumer goods was more appropriate as both sectors were likely to benefit from the weaker yen.
